headline: Low interaction risk: both profiles are non-runnable, network-egress-none open-source lists, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile is runnable, and both expose no I/O surfaces or shared channel. With agent_a.network_egress and agent_b.network_egress both none, there is no documented path for one agent to ingest the other's outputs by default. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore blocked.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF either profile becomes runnable, re-evaluate whether outputs are parsed as instructions.
mitigations: Do not add shared clipboard or filesystem bridges.
Require explicit provenance tags before any cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles touch no data classes and have network_egress set to none, so there is no documented route for sensitive data to leave one agent and reach the other or a third party. Because neither agent is shown to share a workspace or authenticated principal, leakage is not evidenced here.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, re-evaluate leakage.
IF either agent is granted outbound network access, reassess exfiltration risk.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Maintain outbound network egress as none.
Separate credentials and OAuth principals if either agent is later enabled.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented: both io_surfaces and concurrency_model are empty, and both agents are non-runnable with no permissions requested. Without filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write scopes, there is no plausible write-conflict pathway between the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later given write access to the same directory or resource, reassess conflict risk.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, re-evaluate.
mitigations: Add locking before enabling any write-capable integration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pathway where agent_a's output becomes authoritative input to agent_b, because both profiles are non-runnable and expose no I/O surfaces. The email-scheduling category on agent_b does not create a downstream action path here without an enabled integration, so cascading error is not evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_b is wired to consume agent_a outputs automatically, reassess.
IF either agent gains action-taking authority such as sending email or committing changes, re-evaluate.
mitigations: Do not auto-feed outputs between agents.
Insert human verification before any downstream action.
Keep agent_b disconnected from action-taking integrations.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented, and both profiles list no touched data classes. Because the pair is open-source, unverified, and non-runnable with no network egress, there is no evidenced compliance exposure to assign beyond none.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data classes, reassess compliance obligations.
IF deployment introduces residency or retention requirements, re-evaluate against those controls.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data to either agent.
Document residency and retention before deployment.
Keep both agents in a non-production, non-data-processing role.
